title: Sowing Wind, Reaping a Whirlwind
overview: God sounds an alarm against Israel for its idols, its self-made kings and its trust in foreign powers, and warns that disaster is coming.

parts.label: Sound the alarm (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The prophet is told to blow a war trumpet because an enemy, pictured as an eagle or vulture, is swooping on the LORD's house, most likely meaning Israel's land and people. The people still claim to know God, but they have broken their covenant, their binding agreement with him, so the claim rings hollow.

parts.label: Kings and a calf (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: In Hosea's day the northern kingdom went through a string of kings who seized power, often by murder, without seeking God at all. The calf idol at their shrines, first set up by King Jeroboam generations earlier, was just metal shaped by a craftsman, and Hosea says it will be smashed.

parts.label: Wind and whirlwind (vv. 7-10)
parts.note: Israel's empty efforts are like planting wind and harvesting a storm, with failed crops and foreigners eating what little grows. Israel paid the king of Assyria for protection, as if hiring lovers, but will instead waste away under his heavy demands.

parts.label: Altars that became sin (vv. 11-13)
parts.note: Israel built many altars meant to deal with wrongdoing, but this worship went against God's own instructions, so it only added to their guilt, and God rejects the sacrifice meat they enjoy eating. "Return to Egypt" may mean slavery again, as if their ancestors' escape were undone, or it may point to Israelites actually fleeing to Egypt when Assyria invaded.

parts.label: Palaces and forts (v. 14)
parts.note: Both Israel in the north and Judah in the south trusted in grand buildings and walled towns while forgetting the God who made them. Fire would consume those defenses, and Assyrian armies did later destroy Israel and capture many of Judah's fortified towns.

think: Where have you seen small choices grow into consequences far bigger than anyone expected?
